aathira varier Mumbai, 10 November Two working groups have been formed to develop a framework to align the proposed risk-based capital (RBC) regime with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS). Announcing their formation on Tuesday, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai) said the groups, comprising representatives from life and non-life insurers, had been given a month to prepare an exposure draft of the RBC regula- tions and an accompanying approach paper. The life insurance group includes chief ﬁnancial officers or appointed actuaries of Life Insurance Corporation, SBI Life, HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential Life, Bajaj Life, Tata AIA, Kotak Life, Bandhan Life and Aditya Birla Life, along with Munich Re and the Institute of Actuaries of India. The non-life group comprises similar representatives from New India Assurance, ICICI Lombard, Bajaj General, SBI General, Tata AIG, Niva Bupa, IndusInd General and Kiwi General, along with Swiss Re and the Institute of Actuaries of India. Irdai said the two groups would work in close coordination, with joint meetings wherever issues common to life and non-life insurers arose, to ensure a consistent approach across the industry. All deliberations, data, drafts and docu- ments of the groups will remain conﬁdential. The move is aimed at using Ind AS ﬁnan- cial statements as the starting point for cal- culating capital requirements under the proposed RBC framework, with deﬁned adjustments wherever required for pruden- tial purposes. Currently, insurers follow a factor-based solvency regime. Under the proposed RBC framework, an insurer’s capital requirement will be linked to the risks it carries and measured using an economic, or market- consistent, balance sheet. Irdai said running the two frameworks on separate and unconnected bases could increase compliance costs for insurers, create reconciliation complexities, and lead to inconsistent outcomes and regulatory arbitrage. Both frameworks share common measurement principles, including esti- mates of future cash ﬂows, discounting and explicit allowances for risk. The working groups will examine the valuation of assets and liabilities, determin- ing available and required capital, risk mod- ules, calibration standards, and aggregation and diversiﬁcation beneﬁts. They will also assess the treatment of key components such as debt securities and expected credit loss (ECL), the contractual service margin (CSM), risk adjustment for non-ﬁnancial risk, insurance acquisition cash ﬂows, reinsurance contracts and prop- erty valuation. The exercise will also cover differences between Ind AS and the prudential require- ments of the RBC framework, including the construction of risk-free yield curves, dis- counting methodologies, illiquidity pre- miums and alignment the RBC risk margin with the Ind AS risk adjustment. The groups will prepare templates for insurers to submit RBC-related data to the regulator, covering the RBC balance sheet. Irdai forms two working groups on risk-based capital framework
